name: Pullman estate (1800 S. Calumet Avenue): the two-storey stone lodge between the glasshouse ranges

grade.why: Pictured: 2 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the sheet-28 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-28.json, allocation s28-pullman-service-garden) rules the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground and its lodge present in 1904. Its building date, which the census reads off the 1894 conservatory plate, is T-3165's to read from the pictures themselves.

placement.position_note: The north-east corner, read off the committed sheet 28 raster at pixel (3186, 2359) where the drawn wall lines cross, and carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json; 1.47 m RMS on independent standing houses): local E 1470.53, N -3274.69. The bearing turns the plan onto the sheet's own ruled lines (1.014 degrees off east in that fit), so u runs west to the alley and v south, and the building runs square to the lot as drawn.
placement.symbolic_location: 1800 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_1800 (data/street_grid/1904.json): the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground across 18th Street from the house, west side of Calumet Avenue between 18th and 20th Streets; the two-storey building at the angle of the two glasshouse ranges.

footprint.note: u from the east wall west to the alley, v from the north wall south. The drawn lines' centres on the sheet (x 3009-3186, y 2359-2588) at 0.0506 m a pixel: 8.95 by 11.58 m. Its north wall is the north range's south end and its east wall the east range's west end, as the sheet draws them.

stories.note: The sheet prints '2' on the lodge: two storeys.

construction.note: T-3164 re-entered: the 1894 Inland plate shows the lodge's north front in coursed rock-faced stone like the east range it adjoins, not brick; the 1911 sheet's pink wash in its north-west corner is read as the colourist's, as its diagonal run into the glasshouse already was. The sheet's '2' stands.

parts.from: the sheet's lodge outline, read by hand (T-3164); its roof the plate's: a steep hip cut off at a crested lead deck

draft_plan.note: One rectangle, the whole outline: the sheet draws no wing or bay on it. T-3164 re-entered: the roof is the plate's, a steep hip (about 52 degrees) stopped at a flat deck 3.7 m over the eave inside an iron cresting, the deck's north edge reading x 1010-1105 on the plate (2.8 m in from the east eave, 3.1 m from the west); the deck's depth is reconstructed at the same pitch.

draft_elevation.note: T-3164 RE-ENTERED against the 1894 Inland plate (data/reference_views/pullman_glasshouse_1800_calumet_pavilion/inland_1894_conservatory.json; 25.8 px/m at the lodge, grade y 931, its north-east corner at x 948, 25.5 px/m along the front): the north front is a tall ground storey, a loggia of three openings between round columns (dark x 955-967, 977-1003 and 1015-1052, so 0.5, 1.0 and 1.45 m wide at 0.51, 1.65 and 3.35 m west of the east wall, the columns between them about 0.45 m) under an entablature whose underside reads y 812 (4.6 m); a balcony band y 775-795 (5.3-6.0 m) across it; one small upper sash over the middle opening, x 998-1017 and y 751-773 (0.75 m wide, 6.1-7.0 m); and the eave at y 720 (8.2 m), so storeys of 5.5 and 2.7 m over grade. The plate shows no stack on the slopes it sees; the Lowe photograph (c. 1897) shows one rising behind the east slope, so the draft's stack (which the rules had stood on the north-west, in the plate's view) is moved there, 2.4 m in from the east wall and 8 m back, its top 11.8 m (the print's stack top about 15 px under the deck's cresting), its place behind the slope RECONSTRUCTED. T-3164 (third pass): the upper storey's north-east corner turned on a bow (a 1.2 m chord along each wall, 0.1 m proud of the corner, 5.3-8.2 m) with the eave carried round it and belled 0.4 m out and down (the roof's bowed chamfer); a balcony on the loggia's entablature, its floor at 5.3 m and an open balustrade 0.75 m high, 0.45 m deep from 0.2 m east of the corner to 4.2 m along the front, its east end turned on a quarter-round under the bow; two round columns 0.38 m across between the loggia's openings; and the deck in the stable's open cresting with a spire at each corner, as the plate shows them (L-pullman-lodge-front-3164: the bow's plan, the balcony's depth and balusters, the columns' bases and capitals and the cresting's pattern are RECONSTRUCTED). STILL OPEN against the plate: the lower hipped roof over the front's west part (x 1055-1135). UNRESOLVED: neither the plate nor the Lowe photograph shows the lodge's east face or east slope over the east range's coping (both show sky and a railing there), which the sheet's 11.6 m-deep two-storey outline and the two solved cameras, both standing east of the lodge, say should show; either the two-storey block is shallower than the sheet draws or the cameras stand further west than solved, and this record keeps the sheet's outline until that is read. RECONSTRUCTED: the west and south fronts, which no picture shows, keep the draft rules' sash and the south door (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). WHAT T-3164 FIRST BUILT: RECONSTRUCTED on the draft rules' brick-family values: a hipped roof over two storeys, three bays on its alley front with the door at the south end, one stack, no dormers. Nothing describes the lodge beyond the sheet's '2' and 'D' (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164).

function.note: The 1911 sheet letters it 'D', a dwelling, at the angle of the two glasshouse ranges; the sheet-28 census reads it as the estate's gardener's lodge (s28-pullman-garden-lodge, tier reconstructed): nothing names its occupant or use beyond the 1911 'D'.

citations.citation: Inland Architect Press. Conservatory of Geo. M. Pullman, Chicago. S. S. Beman, Architect. Photographic plate in The Inland Architect and News Record, vol. 24, no. 4 (1894). Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives, Archival Image Collection (Inland Architect plates), IA2404_1676.
what_it_supplies: the conservatory's sections, heights and openings through its camera (49.5 px/m on the north front)
the east range's masonry face, windows and coping height, and its round end's colonnade and dome
the north range's north end as a low curved glass roof
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 state: the plate is 1892-94, and the 1911 sheet draws a longer north range than it shows
the south and west sides, and the ranges' roofs behind their parapets

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-3164 (piece 1 of T-1934): built on the district draft's builder (generators/archetypes/prairie_draft.py) because no kit carries a small service dwelling yet, and exempt from the draft rules' re-derivation because the rules' skip names it (as T-2538 did for 1801). Read off sheet 28 by hand: the colour trace would follow this copy's pink wash, which runs diagonally into the east glasshouse range rather than stopping at the lodge's dashed east line. Heights, roof and openings are the draft rules' brick-family values (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). T-3165 refines it to the pictures. T-3164 re-entered (2026-10-28): rebuilt to the 1894 Inland plate's north front, in stone under a crested deck roof; see draft_elevation's note for what the plate still shows that this does not.
